findings.summary: A declaration licenses the whole file with no stated consequence when it fails. "Block only an undeclared change that no line requires" plus "Judge each diff by its declaration, not as weakened" let a reviewer pass: a declared class-1 file that also drops an unrelated assertion (probe B2), a class-1 bullet whose line states no new value (B3), a bare bullet with no requiring line (B4). The 1.8.0 rule blocked all three. Fix in the same section, keeping the brief's "block only undeclared": define declared, e.g. "A declaration covers only the change its line requires and its class proves (class 1: the stated value; class 2: the fault proof; class 3: the ledger row and owner yes). Anything else in the diff is undeclared." Add a probe-style test that a class-1 declaration without a stated value, or with an extra removed assertion, is not covered.

test-changes.mjs reads the spec's current text, so an implementer that adds its own ## Test changes bullet after the base turns an undeclared weakening into a declared one (probe B7: base section "none", implementer adds class 2 and drops an assertion; startup shows declared, undeclared []). The rules never say declarations come from decompose (the spec at the base). Fix: one rule, "A declaration added or changed after the base counts only with a line that requires it; otherwise the change is undeclared", or have test-changes.mjs read the spec at --base.

assumption: payload startup prints testChanges only when the coordinator passes --changes-base; without it nothing is printed (no warning), and this repo's installed .joycraft/runtime/dispatch-start.mjs has no testChanges at all (this review's startup had none). The rule "Read testChanges from startup" needs a fallback: when it is missing, run test-changes.mjs with the spec's base or ask the coordinator, and never read missing as none.

test-changes.mjs uses --no-renames, so a rename shows as one declared and one undeclared path (probe B5) or two undeclared (B6). "A declaration of either path of a rename covers both" is right, but the text does not say how the reviewer sees the pair (git diff -M <base>) or that a rename that drops assertions is class 3, not class 2. With f1 fixed, class 2's fault proof (spec 18) is what catches a hidden deletion.

An undeclared deletion or skip that an acceptance line "requires" passes the block rule without the class-3 ledger row and owner yes. The brief's rule allows this literally; consider "a required change still needs its class condition".

"One bullet per test file the spec changes" reads as covering new test files too, yet this spec adds tests/text-test-changes.test.ts with Test changes: none (correctly passed as undeclared-but-required). Saying "each existing test file" avoids decomposers listing every new test.
